title: Base change and topology of finite morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $Y,X$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:Y\to X$ a morphism which is finite on scheme tests: for every scheme $T\to X$, $Y\times_XT$ is a scheme finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. For every algebraic space $X^{\prime}\to X$, the base change $Y\times_XX^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}$ is finite on scheme tests. The map $|f|:|Y|\to|X|$, with point sets and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], is continuous and closed and has finite fibres. The morphism $f$ is locally quasi-finite: after any etale scheme chart $V\to X$, the scheme morphism $Y\times_XV\to V$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $Y^{\prime}=Y\times_XX^{\prime}$ is an algebraic space. For a scheme $T\to X^{\prime}$, the fibre-product universal property gives $(Y\times_XX^{\prime})\times_{X^{\prime}}T\cong Y\times_XT$, compatibly with projection to $T$: on sections both sides are the pairs $(y,t)$ with $f(y)$ equal to the image of $t$ in $X$. The right side is a scheme finite over $T$ by the hypothesis on $f$. This proves finiteness on scheme tests after the arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 03ZS, lemma-base-change-integral: direct verification on scheme tests

proof.text: Choose, by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], a scheme $V$ and a representable surjective etale map $p:V\to X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] such that $|p|:|V|\to|X|$ is surjective. Put $W=Y\times_XV$ and write $q:W\to Y$, $g:W\to V$. The hypothesis on $f$ makes $W$ a scheme and $g$ finite. For a scheme $T\to Y$, the universal property identifies $T\times_YW$ with $T\times_XV$, the scheme test of $p$ along $T\to Y\to X$; hence $q$ is representable, etale and surjective in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Since $\{p\}$ is jointly surjective on point classes, the etale-cover base-change clause of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $|q|:|W|\to|Y|$ surjective as well. By [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], the topology of $|X|$ (respectively $|Y|$) is the quotient topology of any representable surjective etale map from a scheme, in particular of $p$ (respectively $q$), and $|t|$ is continuous for every morphism $t$ from a scheme. Thus a subset of $|X|$ (respectively $|Y|$) is open, or closed by taking complements, exactly when its inverse image in $V$ (respectively $W$) is open, or closed. This is the atlas topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology].

source.place: Tag 03BX, lemma-topology-points, first paragraph; atlas base change: spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F, lemma-etale (3)

proof.text: For an open $O\subseteq |X|$, $p^{-1}(O)$ is open in $V$. The equality $q^{-1}(|f|^{-1}(O))=g^{-1}(p^{-1}(O))$ follows from $f\circ q=p\circ g$ on field-point classes [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Its right side is open because the scheme morphism $g$ is continuous [def-pc-scheme]. Detection in the atlas $q$ therefore makes $|f|^{-1}(O)$ open in $|Y|$, proving continuity. The atlas topology here is the topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology], described by the quotient topologies of step 2 [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover].

Let $C\subseteq |Y|$ be closed. Its inverse image $q^{-1}(C)$ is closed in $W$. The finite scheme morphism $g$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], so $g(q^{-1}(C))$ is closed in $V$. We claim that this is $p^{-1}(|f|(C))$. One inclusion follows from the commutative square. For the reverse inclusion, take $v\in |V|$ and $y\in C$ with $p(v)=f(y)$. Represent $v$ by its residue-field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$, and $y$ by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$. The point-class definition [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] gives a field $L$ extending both fields such that the two induced maps $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ agree. Their pair is a section of the sheaf fibre product $W$. Its scheme point $w$ satisfies $g(w)=v$ and $q(w)=y$, so $w\in q^{-1}(C)$. Thus $v\in g(q^{-1}(C))$. Closedness is detected by the atlas $p$, by the quotient-topology description of step 2 [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], so $|f|(C)$ is closed. This proves closedness without identifying a fibre product of topological spaces with the point space of a sheaf fibre product.

source.place: Tag 0415, lemma-integral-universally-closed; expanded pointwise atlas descent using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian

proof.text: Fix $x\in |X|$. The atlas $p$ was chosen surjective on point classes [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], so choose $v\in |V|$ over $x$. The scheme fibre set $g^{-1}(\{v\})$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. It maps by $q$ onto $|f|^{-1}(\{x\})$: given $y$ in the latter set, represent $y$ by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ and $v$ by $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$. Since their images represent the same $x$, [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] supplies a common extension field $L$ on which their maps to $X$ agree. The pair over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a section of $W=Y\times_XV$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its scheme point lies over $v$ and maps to the class $y$. Thus the finite scheme fibre surjects onto the required space fibre, which is finite. If $|X|$ is empty there is no $x$ to check.

source.place: Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian, common-field proof; morphisms.tex Tags 02NU and 02NH, finite scheme fibres

proof.text: For any etale scheme chart $T\to X$, the scheme morphism $Y\times_XT\to T$ is finite by the assumed scheme-test condition. Apply [pqf-lem-finite-qf] to this scheme morphism: it is quasi-finite. By [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] a quasi-finite morphism is locally quasi-finite, that is, quasi-finite at each point in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. This holds for every chart, exactly as required by the last clause of the statement.
